title: Deconstructing Large Language Models
subtitle: From Linear Regression to General Intelligence
author: Gen Tang

overview.description: Starting with linear regression, follow the evolution of data foundations and model architectures to gradually understand large language models
overview.seoDescription: Read Deconstructing Large Language Models online: connect linear regression, deep learning, and large language models through data foundations and model architectures, with code examples that illuminate their engineering implementation.

chapter_1.description: Define the data foundation and model architecture of artificial intelligence through the relationship among data, models, and intelligent agents, establishing a high-level perspective for understanding the book’s technical progression.

chapter_2.description: Review the mathematical foundations needed to understand AI models, including vectors, matrices, tensors, probability, and calculus, in preparation for the model derivations and engineering implementations that follow.

chapter_3.description: Use linear regression to understand models, features, loss functions, and parameter estimation, laying the groundwork for progressing from classical statistical models to neural networks and large language models.

chapter_4.description: Use logistic regression to understand binary classification and the combination of nonlinear transformations with linear models, while discussing model implementation, performance evaluation, and multiclass classification.

chapter_5.description: Draw on econometrics to discuss feature engineering, quantitative and qualitative variables, multicollinearity, model stability, and interpretability, refining practical modeling methods.

chapter_6.description: Explore gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, and their variants to understand model parameter estimation, training optimization, and the underlying algorithms of deep learning engineering.

chapter_7.description: Implement backpropagation through computational graphs, forward propagation, and the chain rule, and understand automatic differentiation, GPU computing, and the engineering foundations of neural network training.

chapter_8.description: Build a multilayer perceptron step by step from perceptrons and logistic regression, and understand hidden layers, activation functions, normalization, and the training mechanisms of deep neural networks.

chapter_9.description: Build a CNN from convolution operations and feature extraction, and understand computer vision, GPU training, residual networks, and the key breakthroughs of deep learning.

chapter_10.description: Understand RNNs, LSTMs, word embeddings, and language models for sequential data and natural language, establishing a foundation for attention and large language models.

chapter_11.description: Analyze GPT-2 and LLMs through attention and Transformers, and discuss the core technologies behind pretraining, fine-tuning, LoRA, reward models, and ChatGPT.

chapter_12.description: Understand reinforcement learning, value functions, policy optimization, and PPO through learning in dynamic interactions, connecting reward models, RLHF, and large language model alignment.

chapter_13.description: Broaden the modeling perspective beyond neural networks with decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, hidden Markov models, clustering, dimensionality reduction, and SVD.

parts.label: Part I · Chapters 2–5
parts.title: Foundations of Neural Networks
parts.description: Discuss the cornerstones of neural networks—linear and logistic regression—and introduce general machine learning issues such as overfitting and penalty terms

parts.label: Part II · Chapters 6–12
parts.title: Building ChatGPT from Scratch
parts.description: Begin with optimization algorithms and backpropagation, introduce the core structures of classical neural networks one by one, then implement GPT-2 from scratch and evolve it into ChatGPT

parts.label: Part III · Chapter 13
parts.title: Other Classical Models
parts.description: Briefly introduce other classical models related to neural networks, helping readers understand important modeling ideas beyond neural networks
